questions.scenario: A developer-tools team built an internal service that asks Claude Opus 5.5, through the synchronous Messages API, to generate unit tests for a whole module in one request. The output is a forced `write_tests` tool call whose input is `{ "tests": [ { "function": ..., "file": ..., "code": ... } ] }`, and `max_tokens` is already set to 128000. For modules with more than about 70 exported functions, responses come back with `stop_reason: "max_tokens"` and an incomplete tool_use block, so nothing gets written. Developers trigger the service from their IDE and wait for the result, and module sizes keep growing every quarter. Which change addresses the root cause?
options: Send these large modules through the Message Batches API with the `output-300k-2026-03-24` beta header, which allows up to 300k output tokens.
When `stop_reason` is `max_tokens`, append the partial tool_use as an assistant turn and ask Claude to continue from where it left off.
Add an instruction to keep each generated test under 15 lines and to skip edge cases, so a whole module fits within the 128K output limit.
Split the request into one call per group of related functions, each returning the same `tests` schema, and concatenate the arrays in code.
questions.why_correct: Ya están en el techo de salida del modelo en la API sincrónica y el output crece con el tamaño del módulo: seguir subiendo no es práctico. Partir por grupos de funciones, con el mismo schema en cada llamada, hace que cada respuesta entre cómoda y que el merge sea concatenar arrays.

why_wrong.0: Casi: el beta de 300k existe, pero solo en Batches, que es asincrónico; un dev esperando en el IDE no puede esperar un batch. Y con módulos que crecen, tarde o temprano también queda corto.
why_wrong.1: Para un tool_use truncado, la doc dice reintentar con más `max_tokens`, y acá ya están en el máximo. Continuar un bloque de tool_use a medias no es el patrón documentado.
why_wrong.2: Recorta calidad para entrar en el límite y se vuelve a romper cuando el módulo crezca: trata el síntoma.

questions.rule: Truncado en el techo y output que crece con el input → partir en llamadas chicas con el mismo schema y mergear en código.
questions.source_quote: Break down complex tasks into smaller, consistent subtasks. Each prompt then covers a single subtask, reducing inconsistency errors across scaled workflows.

questions.scenario: A logistics company extracts line items from freight invoices with structured outputs (`output_config.format` with a JSON schema) and `max_tokens: 4096`. About 3% of documents fail with `JSONDecodeError` and are discarded as "invalid model output." Every failing document is a long invoice with 400 to 900 line items; short invoices never fail. The pipeline reads `response.content[0].text` and parses it without looking at any other field of the response. The model and the schema were approved by the data team and cannot change this quarter. What should the team do first?
options: Check `stop_reason`; when it is `max_tokens`, retry with a higher `max_tokens`, which still leaves ample room below the model's output ceiling.
Split every invoice into pages, extract the line items page by page with the same schema, and merge the arrays so no single response gets large.
Wrap the parse in a retry loop that resends the identical request up to three times, since the failures look intermittent across the batch.
Switch from JSON outputs to strict tool use, because strict mode guarantees that the tool input always matches the schema and parses cleanly.
questions.why_correct: Primero el diagnóstico: si `stop_reason` es `max_tokens`, la salida se cortó y por eso no parsea. Con 4096 están lejísimos del techo de 128K, así que subir `max_tokens` es el fix documentado y práctico. Partir la tarea tiene sentido cuando subir ya no alcanza.

why_wrong.1: Funcionaría, pero es sobreingeniería como primer paso: suma llamadas y un merge cuando el problema es un `max_tokens` bajo, no una salida imposible.
why_wrong.2: No es transitorio: el mismo request se vuelve a cortar en el mismo lugar. Reintentar igual es tirar plata.
why_wrong.3: Strict garantiza el schema cuando la respuesta termina; si se corta por `max_tokens`, la salida puede quedar incompleta igual.

questions.rule: Primero mirá `stop_reason`. Lejos del techo → subí `max_tokens`. En el techo → partí la tarea.
questions.source_quote: Retry with a higher `max_tokens` value to get the complete structured output.

questions.scenario: A market-research firm runs a multi-agent system: eight search subagents each return structured findings with citations, and a final synthesis call to Claude Opus 5.5 (synchronous Messages API, `max_tokens: 128000`) rewrites all of them into one JSON report with 12 topic sections. Analysts wait on a live dashboard that must render the report within two minutes. On large projects with 60+ sources, the synthesis response ends with `stop_reason: "max_tokens"` and the last four sections missing. Every finding in the report must keep its citation. Which change is most effective?
options: Move the synthesis call to the Message Batches API with the 300k output beta header, so the full report fits in a single response.
Generate each topic section in its own synthesis call with the same section schema, then assemble the sections into the final report in code.
Prefill the assistant turn with `{"sections": [` so Claude skips any preamble and spends its whole output budget on the report itself.
Instruct the synthesis call to compress each finding into one short sentence and drop secondary sources, so the whole report fits within 128K.
questions.why_correct: La síntesis ya está en el techo sincrónico de 128K y el reporte crece con la cantidad de fuentes. Una llamada por sección, con el mismo schema de sección, mantiene cada salida chica, se puede correr en paralelo para cumplir los dos minutos, y el ensamblado lo hace el código.

why_wrong.0: El beta de 300k existe, pero Batches es asincrónico (la mayoría de los batches termina en menos de una hora): no sirve para un dashboard que tiene que renderizar en dos minutos.
why_wrong.2: El prefill no está soportado en Claude 4.6 y modelos posteriores; y aunque lo estuviera, el preámbulo no es lo que se come 128K.
why_wrong.3: Choca con la restricción: perder fuentes y detalle de citas para entrar en el límite es recortar el producto.

questions.rule: Reporte que crece con el input → generalo por partes y ensamblá en código.
questions.source_quote: Explicit prompt chaining (breaking a task into sequential API calls) is still useful when you need to inspect intermediate outputs or enforce a specific pipeline structure.

questions.scenario: A platform team runs a nightly security audit over 300 repositories. Each repo is sent in one Messages API request that returns a JSON findings report, and a dashboard shows the number of critical findings per repo. To stop parse failures, an engineer added a "JSON repair" library that closes any unterminated arrays and objects before parsing; parse errors dropped to zero. Two weeks later, a pentest found a critical injection flaw in a repo the dashboard had shown with 0 critical findings. That repo's log shows `stop_reason: "max_tokens"` on every nightly run, with about 128,000 output tokens each time. Which change addresses the root cause?
options: Keep the repair library and validate the repaired JSON against the findings schema, so malformed or partial reports are caught before they ever reach the dashboard.
Enable strict tool use for the findings report, so the output is guaranteed to match the schema and no longer needs a repair step.
Instruct Claude to list critical findings first, so that if the response is cut off, only lower-severity findings are lost from the report.
Treat `stop_reason: "max_tokens"` as an incomplete result that is never published, and audit oversized repos with one call per package, merging findings in code.
questions.why_correct: El 'arreglo' escondió el truncamiento: cerrar llaves convierte una salida cortada en un JSON válido pero incompleto. Primero, `stop_reason: "max_tokens"` es un resultado incompleto y nunca se publica como 'sin hallazgos'. Y como ya está en ~128K, el fix estructural es partir por paquete y mergear.

why_wrong.0: El JSON reparado puede cumplir el schema perfectamente: un array de findings más corto es válido. Validar la forma no detecta que falta contenido.
why_wrong.1: Strict asegura el schema de una respuesta completa; no evita que la salida se corte en `max_tokens`.
why_wrong.2: Mitiga, pero el reporte sigue incompleto y se publica como si estuviera completo; y nada garantiza que el modelo ordene perfecto.

questions.rule: `stop_reason: "max_tokens"` = incompleto. Nunca lo 'repares' y publiques: partí la tarea.
questions.source_quote: The output might be incomplete and not match your schema.

questions.scenario: A team runs a blocking pre-merge review: a GitHub Actions job calls Claude Opus 5.5 through the synchronous Messages API and must finish before the PR can merge. Telemetry over 2,000 PRs shows that review output grows roughly linearly with diff size, at about 0.4 output tokens per input token. The job currently sets `max_tokens: 64000`, and the largest diffs (about 470k input tokens) come back truncated. One engineer proposes raising `max_tokens` to 128000; another proposes turning thinking off to free output tokens for the review. Which approach scales to the team's largest PRs?
options: Raise `max_tokens` to 128000, the model's maximum output on the synchronous API, which removes truncation for every PR in the telemetry.
Disable thinking on these requests, so that the whole `max_tokens` budget goes to the review text instead of being shared with thinking.
Split large diffs into per-file review calls within the same job, each with a moderate `max_tokens`, and merge the findings in code.
Move the review to the Message Batches API with the 300k output beta header, and post the findings to the PR when the batch finishes.
questions.why_correct: Con 0,4 tokens de salida por token de entrada, un diff de 470k necesita unos 188k de salida: más que el techo de 128K de la API sincrónica. Ningún `max_tokens` alcanza; partir por archivo mantiene cada salida chica y el job sigue siendo sincrónico.

why_wrong.0: Ayuda con los PR medianos, pero 188k > 128K: los más grandes se siguen cortando. Subir hasta el techo no escala con una salida que crece con el input.
why_wrong.1: En Claude Opus 5.5 el thinking está siempre activo y el adaptive thinking es el único modo: no se puede apagar.
why_wrong.3: Es un check bloqueante pre-merge; Batches es asincrónico y puede tardar hasta 24 horas. Sirve para análisis nocturnos, no para bloquear un merge.

questions.rule: Salida que crece con el input y supera el techo → partir. Subir `max_tokens` solo posterga el problema.
questions.source_quote: Max output: Synchronous Messages API limit.

questions.scenario: A healthcare SaaS reviews pull requests in its 600-service monorepo with one synchronous Messages API call per PR that returns a findings array through a forced tool. Two problems appear on PRs touching 40+ files: responses hit `max_tokens` at 128000, and when they don't, findings contradict each other (the same sanitizer is reported as "missing" in one finding and "correctly applied" in another). The security team insists the review keep catching cross-file taint flows, such as unvalidated input entering a controller in one service and reaching a SQL query in another. Reviews must stay synchronous because they gate merges. Which architecture is most effective?
options: Run focused per-file passes for local issues plus separate integration passes for cross-file data flow, and merge all of the findings in code.
Run one review call per changed file with the same findings schema, then deduplicate and merge the arrays in code into a single report for the PR.
Keep one call per PR but raise the effort level, and add an instruction to double-check that no two findings contradict each other.
Keep one call per PR but send it through the Message Batches API with the 300k output beta header, which removes the truncation.
questions.why_correct: Una sola llamada gigante trunca y diluye la atención (de ahí las contradicciones). Pasadas por archivo para lo local, más pasadas de integración para los flujos entre archivos, cada una con salida chica, y el merge en código. Cubre truncamiento, contradicciones y el requisito de taint entre servicios.

why_wrong.1: Casi: resuelve truncamiento y dilución, pero una pasada por archivo nunca ve el flujo controller → SQL entre servicios. Pierde justo lo que seguridad exige.
why_wrong.2: Más effort no achica la salida ni arregla la dilución de atención de una revisión gigante; siguen en el techo de 128K.
why_wrong.3: Batches es asincrónico y no puede bloquear un merge; y tampoco arregla las contradicciones.

questions.rule: Review grande: pasadas locales por archivo + pasadas de integración entre archivos, merge en código.
questions.source_quote: Splitting large multi-file reviews into focused per-file passes for local issues plus separate integration passes for cross-file data flow analysis

questions.scenario: A health insurer adjudicates hospital bills in near real time: each claim must be extracted and priced within two minutes of upload. Extraction uses Claude Opus 5.5 on the synchronous Messages API with a forced `record_line_items` tool whose input is an array of line items, and `max_tokens` is already 128000. Bills with more than about 2,500 lines (1% of volume, but 30% of claim value) end with `stop_reason: "max_tokens"`. An engineer implemented continuation: append the partial assistant content and send "Please continue from where you left off." The merged results regularly drop or duplicate rows at the seam between responses. Which change addresses the root cause?
options: Retry truncated requests with a higher `max_tokens` value, as the documentation recommends for responses that end with an incomplete tool use block.
Send the large bills through the Message Batches API with the 300k output beta header, and keep the synchronous path for every other bill.
Keep the continuation loop but deduplicate rows by description and amount at each seam, so dropped and repeated rows get reconciled.
Split each large bill into page ranges, extract each range with the same tool schema in parallel calls, and concatenate the arrays in code.
questions.why_correct: Ya están en el techo de salida sincrónico (128K) y la cantidad de filas crece con la factura. Partir por rangos de páginas con el mismo schema, en paralelo, mantiene cada respuesta chica, cumple los dos minutos y el merge es concatenar arrays: ya no hay costuras adentro de una respuesta.

why_wrong.0: La doc lo recomienda, y lejos del techo es lo correcto; pero acá ya están en 128K, el máximo de la API sincrónica. No queda nada para subir.
why_wrong.1: Batches es asincrónico y no garantiza los dos minutos; justo las facturas de más valor quedarían fuera del SLA.
why_wrong.2: Parche sobre un mecanismo frágil: dos filas legítimas iguales (mismo ítem, mismo monto) se borrarían, y las filas perdidas no aparecen deduplicando.

questions.rule: En el techo no estires: partí la entrada y concatená salidas con el mismo schema.
questions.source_quote: Max output: Synchronous Messages API limit.

questions.scenario: A pharmaceutical research team built a literature-review agent. Its final step sends about 900k tokens of full-text papers to Claude Opus 5.5 (1M-token context window) in a single synchronous request with `max_tokens: 64000`, asking for a structured evidence table. On the largest reviews, the response stops after roughly 40k tokens with an incomplete table. The log shows `stop_reason: "model_context_window_exceeded"`. A senior engineer proposes raising `max_tokens` to 128000 and retrying. The team must keep every paper in scope and cannot drop sources. What is the most effective fix?
options: Raise `max_tokens` to 128000, the model's maximum synchronous output, so that the evidence table has twice as much room to finish.
Have subagents extract evidence rows from subsets of the papers in separate calls with the same row schema, then merge the rows in code.
Retry the identical request with exponential backoff, since context window errors are usually transient capacity limits that clear on a later attempt.
Move the request to the Message Batches API with the 300k output beta header, which allows a much longer response for the same input.
questions.why_correct: El `stop_reason` no es `max_tokens`: es `model_context_window_exceeded`. Input más output chocaron con la ventana de 1M. Subir `max_tokens` no crea espacio; repartir los papers entre llamadas (cada una con mucho menos input) y mergear las filas sí, sin descartar fuentes.

why_wrong.0: Lee mal el síntoma: el límite alcanzado es la ventana de contexto, no `max_tokens`. Con 900k de input no queda lugar para más salida.
why_wrong.2: No es un error transitorio sino una respuesta exitosa que se detuvo por el límite de la ventana; el mismo request se corta igual.
why_wrong.3: Los 300k de salida en Batches no agrandan la ventana de contexto: el input de 900k sigue sin dejar lugar.

questions.rule: Mirá cuál `stop_reason` es: `model_context_window_exceeded` se arregla achicando el input por llamada, no con `max_tokens`.
questions.source_quote: Claude stopped because it reached the model’s context window limit.

questions.scenario: An investment research platform runs a coordinator with six subagents (filings, earnings calls, news, patents, hiring, pricing). Each subagent returns a valid JSON object with its findings and citations, about 150k tokens in total. The coordinator then makes one more synchronous call to Claude Opus 5.5, asking it to "merge these six JSON objects into the final report schema, preserving every finding and citation," with `max_tokens: 128000`. That merge call now truncates for most large companies. Analysts watch the report build live and expect it within 90 seconds, and the final report must preserve every citation. Which redesign is most effective?
options: Ask the merge call to shorten each finding to one line and keep only the first citation per finding, so the merged report fits in 128K.
Send the merge call to the Message Batches API with the 300k output beta header, so the full merged report fits in a single response.
Merge the six JSON objects into the report schema in code, and use Claude only for short cross-source parts such as the executive summary.
Prefill the merge response with the report's opening JSON, so the model doesn't spend output tokens restating the schema before the findings.
questions.why_correct: Los subagentes ya devuelven JSON válido: mergear estructuras es trabajo de código, no del modelo. Pedirle al modelo que reescriba 150k tokens de datos es lo que choca con el techo de salida. Claude queda solo para las partes chicas que de verdad requieren síntesis.

why_wrong.0: Rompe la restricción de preservar todas las citas.
why_wrong.1: Batches es asincrónico (la mayoría termina en menos de una hora): no cumple los 90 segundos. Y sigue pagando para que el modelo copie datos que el código mueve gratis.
why_wrong.3: El prefill no está soportado en Claude 4.6 y modelos posteriores; y el problema no es el preámbulo sino reescribir 150k tokens.

questions.rule: Si los datos ya son JSON, el merge lo hace el código. Al modelo, solo lo que necesita síntesis.
questions.source_quote: Break down complex tasks into smaller, consistent subtasks. Each prompt then covers a single subtask, reducing inconsistency errors across scaled workflows.

questions.scenario: A legal-tech company extracts clauses from 5,000 contracts every night. Contracts over 200 pages are split into 6 chunks, and every chunk becomes one request in a single Message Batches API job of about 18,000 requests. The merge step reads the results file line by line and assigns each result to a contract based on the order in which the requests were submitted. Since the switch to batches, auditors find clauses attached to the wrong contract in about 4% of records, and the error rate is higher on nights with larger batches. Every request already uses the same clause schema, and none are truncated. Which change fixes the merge?
options: Give each request a `custom_id` that encodes the contract ID and chunk index, and merge results by `custom_id` instead of by position.
Submit one batch per contract so that each results file contains only that contract's chunks and result order stays aligned with submission order.
Add the contract ID as a required field in the clause schema and ask Claude to copy it from the prompt into every clause it extracts.
Keep each night's batches under 1,000 requests and process them one after another, since result order is only preserved in small batches.
questions.why_correct: Los resultados de un batch pueden volver en cualquier orden. El `custom_id` existe para eso: codificás contrato y chunk (por ejemplo `c48213-chunk3`) y mergeás por ese campo. Es determinístico y no depende del orden.

why_wrong.1: 5.000 batches por noche multiplica la operación, y ni siquiera dentro de un batch el orden está garantizado.
why_wrong.2: Funciona casi siempre, pero confía en que el modelo copie un ID: un dato que ya tenés en tu código no tiene por qué pasar por el modelo.
why_wrong.3: El orden no está garantizado en ningún tamaño de batch; achicarlo solo baja la frecuencia del error y multiplica la operación.

questions.rule: Batches: el orden de los resultados no está garantizado. Mergeá siempre por `custom_id`.
questions.source_quote: Batch results can be returned in any order, and might not match the ordering of requests when the batch was created.
